hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C+D)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C+\blueD A\cdot D$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of seven z squared and a length of six z squared. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is three z and the length is six z squared.  At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative two with a length of six z squared.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{6z^2}(7z^2+3z-2)
\\\\
&=\goldE{6z^2}(7z^2)+\goldE{6z^2}(3z)+\goldE{6z^2}(-2)
\\\\
&=42z^4+18z^3-12z^2
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of seven z squared and a length of six z squared. Inside of this rectangle is forty two z to the fourth power. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is three z and the length is six z squared. Inside of this rectangle is eighteen z cubed. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative two with a length of six z squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative twelve z squared.
